newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FLATTENERS TO FEATURE ON BELGIAN BOND MARKET.
newsitem.headline: FLATTENERS TO FEATURE ON BELGIAN BOND MARKET.

text.p: Volatility looks set to return to the Belgian bond market after a pause on Thursday morning with dealers saying the longer-term trend would be one towards higher interest rates, thus favouring flattening trades.
"There are still people out there looking to sell short and buy long," a trader said. ABN AMRO said, "We advise to take advantage of every serious steepening to put flatteners on."

Analysts said that whatever readings near-term releases of economic indicators might show, interest rate cycles had bottomed out, meaning the short end of yield curves was "out" too. The fate of the longer end depended on inflation trends.

Markets will be offered the latest on the state of inflation in the U.S. with the 1230 GMT release of CPI figures for July. The data are part of a batch of U.S. numbers expected to rekindle activity after a dull Thursday morning.
Dealers said weekly jobless statistics, also due this afternoon, would be closely monitored as well as business inventories and output and capacity use.

One analyst said, "the focus on growth in the U.S." Markets expected a friendly CPI number given the 0.1 percent decline in PPI reported on Wednesday. "CPI at 0.3 percent or higher will be negative," he added, "Jittery markets will prevail."
"If CPI comes out at 0.5 percent, then we all know where markets are headed," a Belgian trader said.
Such a number would add to the unease triggered by the possibility that the Bundesbank might raise interest rates to keep German inflation in check, dealers said.

"Optimism has been dented," an analyst said, "the Belgian economy is particularly sensitive to the prospects of a turnaround in the European interest rate cycle with its high levels of public debt...this would mainly affect the short end. At the long end fundamentals are pretty sound with the inflation outlook subdued."
He recommended being short marks, long European periferals, or better still long dollars.
